difficultyRationale: Requires picking the fix that actually removes the compile-time dependency on a concrete class rather than one that only works around it.
explanation: Depending directly on a concrete implementation couples InvoiceService to every detail of MySqlInvoiceRepository, including its need for a real database connection. Depending on an interface instead, with the concrete implementation supplied from outside, lets any implementation -- a test double, an in-memory store, or a different database -- be substituted without changing InvoiceService.

options.text: Keep MySqlInvoiceRepository, but mark its methods protected so InvoiceService can override them in tests.
options.explanation: Overriding protected methods still requires subclassing the concrete MySQL-specific class, so tests and alternate backends remain tied to its implementation details; the coupling to the concrete class is not removed.

options.text: Add a boolean flag to MySqlInvoiceRepository that switches its internal logic between 'test mode' and 'production mode', still requiring a live MySQL connection whenever the flag is accidentally left in production mode.
options.explanation: This keeps InvoiceService coupled to one concrete class and pushes the problem inside that class instead, mixing two unrelated behaviors behind a flag rather than separating them behind an interface.

options.text: Have InvoiceService depend on an InvoiceRepository interface injected from outside (for example, via its constructor), and let MySqlInvoiceRepository be one implementation chosen at startup.
options.explanation: Depending on a concrete implementation couples InvoiceService to every detail of MySqlInvoiceRepository, including its need for a real database; depending on an interface instead lets any implementation -- a test double, an in-memory store, or a different database -- be substituted without changing InvoiceService.

options.text: Duplicate InvoiceService into TestInvoiceService, which calls a hardcoded in-memory list instead of MySqlInvoiceRepository.
options.explanation: Duplicating the service class to swap one dependency means every future change to InvoiceService's real logic must be repeated in the test copy, trading tight coupling for duplicated business logic.
